analysis.title: European Morning Note
key_insights: US equities fell for a second day on Friday as oil rose and technology megacaps treaded water after Thursday's selloff (-0.5%). The SOX ended +0.4%.

WTI crude rose 3.9% to above $103 a barrel as conflict in Saudi Arabia intensified. Brent has since retreated toward $114 (-1.6%) as Qatari mediators visit Tehran and Trump frames the choice as deal or renewed strikes.
Yields on 10-year Treasuries rose to 5.00% on Friday and are back below 5% this morning. Consumer confidence fell to a five-month low as inflation expectations rose.
US futures are +20-30bps. VGZ6 is +0.4% in early trading.

Asia is soft under the surface but recovering off early lows, with Korea/memory and Chinese AI names lagging. Fanuc (+1.3%) was upgraded on data-centre and semiconductor demand. NK225 -1.1%, HSI +0.4%.
Brazil is the major idiosyncratic risk after Lula's surprise victory. A Brazil ETF listed in Japan fell 16%.
French risk should see small relief today after Moody's kept France's rating at Aa3 and avoided the expected downgrade.

The week ahead is described as binary. Oil is providing some relief but tails remain. Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon need to show AI cash generation can catch up with capex. FOMC is Wednesday, ECB Thursday and BoJ Friday.
US clocks have not changed yet (Nov 1), so the US cash open is at 13:30 London time this week.
